structured.approach: I read both contracted inputs (feat.tasks and feat.design) to find the Data Science tasks (TSK-03 and TSK-04 in ap_forecast) and the design's rules on storage. Then I read each ap_forecast module I cite (__init__.py, predict.py, explain.py and models.json) to confirm that none of them uses a database. I cite each file by its own path rather than by its directory. Finally I wrote task.db_changes, which records an empty list of required database changes with evidence for each point. I used no connectors or subagents because the inputs, the tool view and the four files already answer the question.

claims.text: The Data Science lane has two tasks in ap_forecast: TSK-03 (STORY-03, risk.vendor_risk) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, build_explanation_request with risk=None).
The design puts storage, databases and schema migrations out of scope. Data in this feature stays in memory or travels as CT-1 JSON.
DD-1 adds no new repository, service, runtime, library or storage, and NF-10 requires every new function to be pure and in-memory with no I/O.
TSK-03 makes no LLM call, makes no network call and does not read models.json. TSK-04 must not change models.json.
Any storage or network call from the libraries would re-trigger DES-01, and this design triggers none of the re-triggers.
ap_forecast has no database. No migrations exist and none are required.
predict.py computes a rounded mean over an in-memory history, and explain.py reads only the local models.json and builds a request dict. Neither opens a database connection.
models.json is the LLM provider configuration (provider, model, max_tokens) that explain.load_config reads. It is not a database.

structured.summary: TSK-03 and TSK-04 in ap_forecast need no database changes, so none are left to complete. The design rules out storage and migrations (A1, DD-1, NF-10, A8), and the tool view confirms ap_forecast has no database or migrations. I read the four package files I cite and none of them uses a database. models.json is LLM configuration, not a database. task.db_changes has been rewritten in full with each file cited by its own path. There are no open questions.
